title: Cris Pop: The road from knowing to becoming, a personal growth framework
summary: Cris Pop argues school fills heads with information but doesn't teach you to build or change. He shares the personal framework he built to outgrow mediocrity: an honest inventory, forgiving and accepting your past, a scout mentality, and small intentional daily steps. Mostly mindset, with little on business tactics.

principles.text: Learning counts only when you put it into practice and live it, not when you store facts.
principles.quote: Learning starts the moment we take ownership of it, when we stop treating knowledge like something to collect and start treating it like something to live.

principles.text: Put intention and passion into your work even if it wasn't your passion at first, or you'll extract only disappointment.
principles.quote: It wasn't my passion at first, but I allowed myself to put passion into what I do because without intention and fire in your work or learning, you'll extract nothing but disappointment.

principles.text: When a task feels too hard, commit to a fixed 1-2 year trial and give it everything before judging.
principles.quote: On my first day coding, I wanted to quit. It was too hard, too confusing. But I made myself a promise: give it everything for 1-2 years and see if I was up for the challenge.

principles.text: Seek mentors, absorb what they offer, apply what fits you, then become a mentor yourself.
principles.quote: I hunted for mentors, people willing to help because when you're truly paying attention, you can learn from anyone walking a similar path.

principles.text: Be a scout, not a soldier: question your beliefs and be willing to be wrong to find the truth.
principles.quote: Stop being a soldier who fights to prove everyone else wrong and start being a scout who's willing to be wrong if it means finding the truth.

principles.text: Take an honest inventory of where you stand, then invest in what you want through small daily steps.
principles.quote: It takes brutal honesty about where we stand, the humility to unlearn what doesn’t serve us, and the courage to take small but intentional steps every day.
